doc.title: Longineu Parsons interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 17, 2026

title: Louis Armstrong tributes and his younger son in Taiwan
summary: Parsons does Louis Armstrong tributes and quartet gigs, and spends summers playing in Taiwan with his younger son, a jujitsu champion.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: What’s up next for you? You have concerts you do at A&M or you’re constantly lining up gigs for yourself?

Yes, yes. Okay I have a few different things going. One thing is I’m doing these Louis Armstrong tributes. And those are going very well. And I was somewhat rejecting that, trying not to do those things anymore, but then I realized if I’m going to do a tribute to somebody else at least I’m fortunate enough to be doing it to the greatest of all time. The © Fillius Jazz Archive -15-

great Louis Armstrong who I admire not just as a musician but as a person. Okay, and so other than that I also, I have my quartet things that I get booked and I go to Asia during summers and play in a club there in Taiwan and hang out with my son who lives there.
He’s two times national jujitsu champion of Taiwan.
